name: ANSI three-input NOR gate
summary: Three-input OR outline with an output bubble; the output is high only when all three inputs are low.
description: The three-input NOR gate is the OR outline with three inputs and a bubble at the pointed output. The output is high only when all inputs are low. Triple three-input NOR packages provide the function and it is often used to create an all-clear signal.
When all inputs are themselves active-low alarm lines, the same function may be easier to read as an AND outline with bubbled inputs. A consistent choice across the drawing set makes reviews quicker.
The symbol does not show output drive strength or whether the output may be wired to others. Check the device type before connecting outputs together.
readingNotes: Look for the output bubble at the point of the outline.
Check whether a De Morgan form is used elsewhere for the same signal.
drawingChecklist: Name the condition each input represents.
Note the device section and pin numbers.
distinction: An AND outline with three bubbled inputs is the De Morgan equivalent of this gate.
